intro.value: The national park campground at Skaftafell sits below Vatnajökull, Europe's largest glacier, beside the trails to Svartifoss and Skaftafellsjökull. It has been on this spot since 1974. It is open year-round with no reservations; in winter only zones A and C (vehicle access and electricity) stay open. It is the only campsite between Kirkjubæjarklaustur (70 km west) and Höfn (130 km east) that publishes a year-round season.

address.value: Skaftafellsstofa, 785 Öræfi (campground entrance on the west side, off Route 1)

winter.value: Open all year. In winter only zones A and C stay open (vehicle access, separate pitches, electricity). No water at the outdoor sinks until about mid-May because of frost; water is available indoors. In winter, register at the reception in the Skaftafellsstofa Visitor Centre.

applies_to.value: 2026 rates per person per night, accommodation tax included

items.label: Do overnight campground guests also pay the regional (parking) fee?
items.note: The sources checked don't say. There is no vehicle fee on the campsite price list.

items.label: Regional (parking) fee at Skaftafell car park, per day
items.value: 1,110 ISK (car, 5 or fewer seats); 1,440 ISK (6–9 seats); valid until midnight on the day paid

electricity.value: Yes – 100 electrical outlets in zones A–D; A and C (open in winter) have separate pitches and good access to electricity. 1,500 ISK per 24 h. Not for charging vehicles: the park says the system is neither powerful nor safe enough.

kitchen.value: No indoor dining or cooking facilities for campground visitors. Dishwashing sinks next to the service buildings (no outdoor water until about mid-May). The Visitor Centre has food service.

showers.value: Included in the campsite fee (2026). An older Visit Vatnajökull page still describes paid service cards; the national park's own 2026 price list says showers are included.

dump_station.value: Listed by tjalda.is ('Waste disposal for mobile homes'). The national park's own campground page does not mention it, so ask at reception where it is.

wifi.value: Wi-Fi is listed as a service; free internet access at the Skaftafell Visitor Centre

laundry.value: Washing machine and dryer, included in the campsite fee

camping_card.value: No – Skaftafell is not among the campsites in the Útilegukortið (Camping Card) 2026 list.

contact.value: +354 470 8300 · skaftafell@nattura.is · vatnajokulsthjodgardur.is. No reservations (campsites cannot be booked); pay on site.

practical.value: You can't reserve a pitch. Register and pay at the camping reception before you set up; the campsite fee is paid on site, not in the Parka app.
Vehicles can only enter the campsite between 07:00 and 23:00. Quiet hours are 23:30–07:00.
Winter reception is in the Skaftafellsstofa Visitor Centre. Its hours: November 9–17, December–February 10–17, March–May 9–17, September–October 9–18, June–August 9–19.
Zones E, F, G and H are tent-only (no driving). Campervans use A–D, and in winter only A and C.
The area is accessible year-round, 'weather and road conditions permitting'. Outside summer, conditions can change rapidly, so check before you drive.
Collecting firewood in the national park is prohibited. Dogs are allowed but must be on a leash. Sort waste at the stations in the centre of the campsite and by the Visitor Centre.
Nearest towns: Kirkjubæjarklaustur 70 km west and Höfn 130 km east.
